documents.unit: Office of the Provost (AI Vision Committee)
documents.title: Policies and Principles on Using Generative AI Tools in Education
documents.stance_why: The proposal offers three templates, "a No-AI approach", "Limited-AI" and "Full-AI", and says faculty "should be encouraged" to state their own expectations in the syllabus. It sets no university-wide default, so stance is delegates with the tiers listed.
documents.summary: A July 2023 committee proposal setting out Fordham's AI literacy, classroom, assessment and integrity recommendations. It offers three sample syllabus statements (No-AI, Limited-AI, Full-AI) and leaves the choice to instructors, with no rule of its own.

units.why: The introduction says there is "a legitimate concern that students will exploit GAI for academic dishonesty or cheating", a rationale about misuse. No type covers a bare concern about student dishonesty (P36 needs a classification or process, P41 is about skill building), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: there is a legitimate concern that students will exploit GAI for academic dishonesty or cheating
units.uncovered_note: Rationale statement that students may exploit generative AI for academic dishonesty.

units.why: Says "when used properly, students can leverage GAI to enhance their critical thinking skills by engaging in interactive discussions", an affirmative rationale; interactive discussion for understanding fits P12 (tutor for understanding) better than P44 (professional skill).
units.anchor: students can leverage GAI to enhance their critical thinking skills by engaging in interactive discussions

units.why: States GAI "can aid in improving writing abilities by providing suggestions, grammar corrections, and even generating draft content", naming permissible prose uses, so P18 (prose separate from code).
units.anchor: GAI can aid in improving writing abilities by providing suggestions, grammar corrections

units.why: Says GAI helps "in the creation and debugging of computer programs" and can "lower barriers" for non-specialist courses; a favourable statement about code use, P13 as debugging is named, P16 would need conditions.
units.anchor: creation and debugging of computer programs

units.why: Sets the principle "to maintain a balance between leveraging AI tools for support and preserving the authenticity and originality of student work", an institution-level principle, so P56.
units.anchor: preserving the authenticity and originality of student work to uphold academic integrity

units.why: States the committee objective to "harness the potential of GAI as a valuable educational resource while safeguarding the principles of academic integrity", a purpose statement for the framework, so P56.
units.anchor: harness the potential of GAI as a valuable educational resource

units.why: Names "bias and fairness in AI-generated content", unequal access and harms to democracy, which are ethical and bias concerns, so P53; P51 is about providing access, which this sentence does not do.
units.anchor: concerns regarding bias and fairness in AI-generated content

units.why: Says Fordham "has an opportunity to help students develop AI literacy to evaluate the implications of GAI tools and, thus, use them ethically and responsibly", a commitment to teach responsible use, so P44.
units.anchor: help students develop AI literacy to evaluate the implications of GAI tools

units.why: Frames Jesuit values ("Cura Personalis", RomeCall) as the basis to "prioritize AI ethics, social justice inclusivity, and individual well-being", an institution-level principle, so P56.
units.anchor: Fordham can prioritize AI ethics, social justice inclusivity, and individual well-being

units.why: Says "it is essential to educate students to use GAI responsibly and ethically", an education commitment about responsible use, so P44.
units.anchor: it is essential to educate students to use GAI responsibly and ethically

units.why: Recommends administration "request the academic integrity committee to review and update the integrity statement", a revision of policy, so P54.
units.anchor: Request the academic integrity committee to review and update the integrity statement.

units.why: Recommends deans "disseminate a statement regarding the responsible use of generative AI tools to faculty members", an institution-wide statement; P09 is about syllabus statements so P56 fits better.
units.anchor: disseminate a statement regarding the responsible use of generative AI tools to faculty members

units.why: Asks chairs and directors to "revisit their learning goals in light of rapid advances in GAI", a curriculum redesign request, so P35.
units.anchor: revisit their learning goals in light of rapid advances in GAI

units.why: Recommends to "Organize workshops on GAI literacy for faculty members", faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: Organize workshops on GAI literacy for faculty members

units.why: Recommends "a dedicated point of contact for faculty members" on technology and teaching strategies for GAI, faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: Designate a dedicated point of contact for faculty members

units.why: Recommends "technical support and guidance to students, faculty, and staff on the effective utilization of GAI" via tutorials and workshops, teaching effective AI use, so P44 (P63 is faculty-only).
units.anchor: technical support and guidance to students, faculty, and staff on the effective utilization of GAI

units.why: Says integrity statements "will provide frameworks for students to identify the use of GAI in completing the course work", i.e. students disclose AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: frameworks for students to identify the use of GAI in completing the course work

units.why: Says faculty identify GAI use "in research and other scholarly publications" and recommends involving "the IRB and University Research Council", governing AI in research, so P62.
units.anchor: involving the IRB and University Research Council to ensure the responsible

units.why: Recommends "a dedicated forum, such as a center, consortium" where faculty share AI teaching strategies, a faculty community, so P63.
units.anchor: Establish a dedicated forum, such as a center, consortium, or other centrally administered unit

units.why: Sample FAQ question asks about tools "to detect AI-generated content, and why are they not so great?", signalling detector weakness, so P39 (as a planned FAQ topic, modality informs).
units.anchor: Are there tools to detect AI-generated content, and why are they not so great?

units.why: A planned FAQ item "Are there guidelines for citing and attributing AI-generated content?" shows citation guidance will be provided, a communication plan; no rule is stated, so P56 over P24.
units.anchor: Are there guidelines for citing and attributing AI-generated content?

units.why: The "No-AI" sample statement says "Generative AI tools are not permitted in this course", a default ban for the course, so P01.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are not permitted in this course.

units.why: The No-AI statement says "Students [or learners] must rely on their own originality, creativity and critical thinking skills", i.e. AI must not replace their thinking, so P32.
units.anchor: Students [or learners] must rely on their own originality, creativity and critical thinking skills

units.why: The Limited-AI sample says use "may be allowed for specific assignments ... when explicitly permitted by the instructor", assignment-level instructor permission, so P04 (P05 is the tier naming, coded separately).
units.anchor: may be allowed for specific assignments in this course

units.why: The proposal offers statements for "a No-AI approach", "Limited-AI" and "Full-AI", three named tiers for syllabi, so P05; the document stance is delegates.
units.anchor: the committee offers the following statements for inclusion in course syllabi

units.why: The Limited-AI sample says "it is mandatory to clearly indicate the sections of your work that were generated", per-submission disclosure, so P24.
units.anchor: it is mandatory to clearly indicate the sections of your work that were generated

units.why: The Limited-AI sample also requires students to "indicate the prompts and software versions that were used", specific citation details, so P25 (the sections-marking rule is P24).
units.anchor: indicate the prompts and software versions that were used

units.why: Limited-AI sample: "adhere to ethical standards by refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content" is a general conduct duty on permitted use. It fits no type (P19 would need AI producing submitted work, P36 a classification), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content
units.uncovered_note: General duty to adhere to ethical standards and avoid plagiarism or misleading content when AI use is permitted.

units.why: Limited-AI sample: "Additional guidelines or restrictions will be provided for specific assignments", detail set per assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: Additional guidelines or restrictions will be provided for specific assignments.

units.why: The Full-AI sample says "This course allows the use of generative AI tools to facilitate exploration of innovative ideas", a default permit, so P02.
units.anchor: This course allows the use of generative AI tools to facilitate exploration of innovative ideas

units.why: The Full-AI sample says "Students must clearly indicate the sections of the work that were generated", per-submission disclosure, so P24.
units.anchor: Students must clearly indicate the sections of the work that were generated

units.why: Full-AI sample, same sentence, also requires students to "indicate the prompts and software versions that were used", a citation-detail rule in this tier's template, so P25.
units.anchor: indicate the prompts and software versions that were used

units.why: Full-AI sample repeats the ethics duty: "refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content", uncovered as in the Limited-AI template.
units.anchor: refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content
units.uncovered_note: General duty to adhere to ethical standards and avoid plagiarism or misleading content when AI use is permitted.

units.why: Suggested assignment where students "revise and edit AI-generated texts" and "submit both the original AI draft and their final version", an AI-based assignment design with drafts, so P35.
units.anchor: Students will submit both the original AI draft and their final version.

units.why: Suggests "in-class presentations comparing and contrasting AI writing with human writing", an AI-embracing assignment, so P35.
units.anchor: Organize in-class presentations comparing and contrasting AI writing with human writing.

units.why: Suggests students "compose variations of the same prompt to fine-tune AI-generated results", an assignment teaching prompt use, so P35.
units.anchor: having students compose variations of the same prompt to fine-tune AI-generated results

units.why: Suggests "encouraging students to interact with AI, using it for brainstorming or divergent thinking exercises", brainstorming use, so P15.
units.anchor: using it for brainstorming or divergent thinking exercises

units.why: Suggests to "Require oral presentation of coursework to assess students' understanding", checking understanding orally, so P34.
units.anchor: Require oral presentation of coursework to assess students' understanding

units.why: Suggests "interactive, in-class exercises" to deter GAI use, moving evaluation into class, so P33.
units.anchor: Employ interactive, in-class exercises to promote active learning

units.why: Suggests case studies on current events as "a short-term defense" that web search "may erode", an assignment redesign against AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Engage in case studies based on current events.

units.why: Says existing tools "are highly imperfect", may miss AI text and "inaccurately identify work by non-native writers", an unreliable-detector statement, so P39.
units.anchor: existing tools are highly imperfect

units.why: For AI-prohibited assignments suggests to "Assess the uniqueness of content using plagiarism detection tools", a similarity check, so P40 (the caveat about accuracy is coded under P39).
units.anchor: Assess the uniqueness of content using plagiarism detection tools or comparison with existing sources.

units.why: Suggests to "Compare the quality and creativity of take-home assignments with in-class work", comparing against in-class evidence to find misuse, so P40.
units.anchor: Compare the quality and creativity of take-home assignments with in-class work

units.why: For AI-allowed assignments, suggests to "Prompt students to reflect on GAI's benefits and limitations", a reflection on AI use, so P26.
units.anchor: Prompt students to reflect on GAI's benefits and limitations, justifying their responses.

units.why: Suggests to "Require students to submit the prompts used for GAI", submitting prompts, so P26.
units.anchor: Require students to submit the prompts used for GAI

units.why: Appendix I rubric helps educators "review assignment prompts for vulnerabilities to generative AI tools", an assignment redesign tool, so P35.
units.anchor: review assignment prompts for vulnerabilities to generative AI tools

units.why: Recommends faculty "incorporate a dedicated section in their course syllabi" on GAI use, a syllabus statement recommendation, so P09 with modality should.
units.anchor: incorporate a dedicated section in their course syllabi

units.why: Faculty should reconsider assignments so "assessments can be designed to reduce the temptation of cheating", an assessment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: assessments can be designed to reduce the temptation of cheating

units.why: Asks that program goals consider "appropriately preparing students for post-graduation studies and careers in a world with these tools", a career rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: appropriately preparing students for post-graduation studies and careers in a world with these tools

units.why: Says "The Writing Center should lead campus discussions on the responsible integration of generative AI tools", including training, support activity, so P63.
units.anchor: The Writing Center should lead campus discussions on the responsible integration of generative AI tools

units.why: Says the Academic Integrity Statement "will be carefully reviewed and updated" to address generative AI, a revision commitment, so P54.
units.anchor: will be carefully reviewed and updated to align with the evolving academic landscape

units.why: The revision will "clarify the expectations and consequences regarding academic integrity violations", treating violations under integrity standards, so P36 (no specific penalty, so not P37).
units.anchor: clarify the expectations and consequences regarding academic integrity violations

units.why: "Deans will inform all students" with "clear guidelines and expectations regarding the use of generative AI tools", an institution-wide communication, so P56 (not syllabus-based, so not P09).
units.anchor: Deans will inform all students based on the outcome of a)

units.why: Recommends "allocating internal funding" for research on AI ethical and social impacts. This is about AI research support, not any AI-use rule; P62 governs AI rules in research, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the committee suggests allocating internal funding from the Office of Research or Deans' grants
units.uncovered_note: Recommendation to fund and hire for research on AI's ethical and social impacts (institutional research investment, not an AI-use rule).

units.why: Cites the need for "the expected AI literacy of graduates" given predicted job loss, a career rationale for teaching AI literacy, so P44.
units.anchor: the expected AI literacy of graduates

units.why: Proposes "workshops ... for educating our neighbors, fostering AI literacy", public AI literacy, so P44.
units.anchor: offer workshops and other interactive initiatives for educating our neighbors, fostering AI literacy

documents.title: Fordham Policy on AI
documents.stance_why: The page states no use rule; it says the committee was set up "to substantively assess the policies, strategies and safeguards" and links its proposal, so it hands decisions elsewhere (delegates).
documents.summary: An IT page that serves as Fordham's AI policy landing page; it only states why the AI Vision Committee was created and links the committee proposal. It adds no rule of its own.

units.why: The IT policy page says the committee was set up "to substantively assess the policies, strategies and safeguards" for GAI in teaching and research, a framework statement of purpose, so P56.
units.anchor: to substantively assess the policies, strategies and safeguards with which Fordham could leverage

documents.title: Standards of Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: It says students complete work "without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools) unless directly authorized by the instructor", which is banned unless explicitly permitted, so restrict.
documents.summary: Fordham's Standards of Academic Integrity require students to do work without outside help including AI tools unless the instructor authorizes it. AI-completed work not expressly permitted counts as plagiarism or falsification.

units.why: Students must complete work "without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools)" unless authorized. This is a default ban, P01; the same sentence also names the instructor exception, coded as P04.
units.anchor: without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools)

units.why: The exception "unless directly authorized by the instructor" leaves the decision for AI use to the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: unless directly authorized by the instructor

units.why: Failing integrity duties brings "sanctions ranging from a reduction in grade, course failure in the assignment, or expulsion", stated penalties, so P37.
units.anchor: sanctions ranging from a reduction in grade, course failure in the assignment, or expulsion

units.why: "It is the student's responsibility to give credit to any quotation, idea, or data used from an outside source", a duty to credit sources (AI is among external resources in the prior sentence), so P24.
units.anchor: It is the student's responsibility to give credit to any quotation, idea, or data

units.why: "It is strongly recommended that instructors place the above paragraph in their syllabi", a syllabus statement recommendation, so P09 with should.
units.anchor: It is strongly recommended that instructors place the above paragraph in their syllabi.

units.why: "GAI policies should be included as well, as per the recommended language by Fordham's AI Vision's Committee", a GAI syllabus statement recommendation, so P09.
units.anchor: GAI policies should be included as well, as per the recommended language

units.why: Plagiarism includes presenting work prepared by "generative artificial intelligence when not expressly permitted", classifying unauthorized AI work as plagiarism, so P36 (P19 would be the student ban; this sentence defines misconduct).
units.anchor: or generative artificial intelligence when not expressly permitted;

units.why: Falsification includes "the usage of artificial intelligence to complete an assignment claimed to be one's own", classifying AI-completed work as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: the usage of artificial intelligence to complete an assignment claimed to be one's own.

notes: IT policy page (fordham-it-policy-ai) is a landing page reproducing/linking the AI Vision proposal, so few units. Integrity-standards cheating items on unauthorized devices/materials do not name AI and were not coded. Course syllabi deferred by collector.
